newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond yields edge lower post-tender.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond yields edge lower post-tender.

text.p: Long-dated Australian bond yields edged lower in immediate response to today's result of a A$600 million Treasury bond tender.
"Interest was fairly wide spread. Everyone was short of 2006s and 2009s, so it was a pretty good tender, and shouldn't take too long to digest," said one trader at a European bank.
The December 10-year bond futures contract touched a high of 92.850 on the result, having stood at 92.830 when final bids went in during the lunchtime recess.

The A$200 million offered in the November 2006 stock, the current 10-year benchmark, fetched a weighted average yield of 7.144 percent with bids ranging from 7.13 to 7.15 percent. The oustanding stock was seen quoted at around 7.16/7.12 percent when bids were submitted.
The accepted bid range was even tighter for the A$400 million September 2009 issue at 7.27 to 7.28 percent, bringing an average yield of 7.277 percent.
This stock, which was first offered at the last tender in October, was seen quoted at around 7.29/7.25 percent pre-tender.
The Australian market has seen strong offshore demand in recent weeks due to current bond friendly fundamentals which left the market short of stock, particularly at the long-end.
This bullish tone was also helped by a more positive U.S. bond market, and helped to push long yields to their lowest level since February 1994 last week at just above 7.0 percent.
However, traders felt that given the U.S. market also faces supply over the next two days, further rallies in the short-term may be constrained.

The tender was the fifth instalment of the Treasury's T-bond issuance programme for the 1996/97 fiscal year, bringing supply to some A$3.6 billion out of a projected A$6.0 to A$7.0 billion projected for the period.

Another tender is expected in three weeks time given that the Treasury said two weeks ago that is expected to hold two tenders before the end of the year, and traders feel they would want to get the second one away before the market settles in for the Christmas/New Year lull.

Bond prices had got off on a softer footing initially ahead of the tender, while a 1.0 percent rise for October merchandise imports, released this morning, was much in line with expectations and had minimal impact on the market.
